title: Add policy-evaluator client w/ scoped safe caching + metrics
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Internal-only: introduces policy-evaluator client library with safe scoped caching and metrics. No external API changes.
description:
Context: As part of RBAC v2 rollout we are moving request-time authorization checks into Gateway + Control Plane services. The policy evaluation path (subject + action + scope -> allow/deny) currently calls the Policy Evaluator service per request. That is correct but adds avoidable latency and load, especially for streaming endpoints where the check happens on initial request handling and can be a noticeable slice of p95 for short prompts.

This PR introduces a shared policy-evaluator client library with scoped caching, bounded memory, and metrics. The core goal is to make caching safe-by-default (no stale allow after role/binding changes) while still capturing the obvious wins (repeat decisions for the same subject/scope/action during bursts).

What’s included (high level): 1) New package `internal/authz/policyclient` providing a typed interface around the evaluator RPC/HTTP endpoint. 2) Scoped cache with TTL + revision pinning. Cache keys include: subject_id, subject_type, org_id, scope (project_id/environment_id/cluster_id), action, and `authz_revision` (aka policy/bindings revision) returned by the evaluator. This ensures entries are not reused across role/binding changes. 3) Safe caching defaults: cache is enabled by default in services that opt-in to the client, with a small TTL (default 5s) and bounded size (default 10k entries). A “no-cache” mode can be enforced by the caller for sensitive flows (e.g. break-glass / impersonation) and for request contexts that set `X-Redwood-Authz-Debug: 1` (to reduce confusion while debugging). 4) Metrics and tracing: `authz_policy_eval_latency_ms` (histogram), `authz_policy_eval_requests_total` (counter), `authz_policy_eval_cache_hits_total` / `..._misses_total`, `authz_policy_eval_cache_entries` (gauge), and cache hit ratio in logs at INFO every N seconds. Traces propagate request_id and include cache hit/miss as span attributes. 5) Benchmark notes + a small load-test harness (non-prod) to measure the impact on Gateway p50/p95 under a realistic request distribution.

Design notes: We considered caching raw role bindings locally, but that pushes more invalidation complexity into each service. Instead, we cache the final decision keyed by `authz_revision`, which is the evaluator’s responsibility to bump on any relevant change (role edit, binding edit, policy bundle update). This aligns with ADR-015 (central evaluation) while still letting us avoid repeat network hops. Invalidation: Because revision is part of the key, explicit invalidation is not required for correctness. TTL is used to bound growth for high-cardinality subjects and to avoid long-lived entries if something goes wrong with revision bumps. Deny caching: We cache both allow and deny decisions. Denies are frequently repeated (e.g., an operator clicking around Console) and caching reduces noisy load. Security: A stale deny is acceptable UX-wise; a stale allow is not. Revision-keying prevents stale allow when revisions are bumped properly; we also cap TTL and emit a warning log if we observe repeated allows under a constant revision for >24h (should not happen outside dev).

Performance (bench notes): On a synthetic Gateway workload (80% chat/completions, 20% management endpoints) with ~2k RPS and typical burstiness, the client reduced evaluator QPS by ~62% and reduced Gateway authz overhead p95 from ~1.4ms to ~0.35ms (excluding network jitter). For streaming routes specifically, time-to-first-byte improves slightly because authz is on the critical path; the effect is more visible for short responses.

Follow-ups: This PR only adds the client library + harness and does not flip it on globally. Subsequent PRs will wire this into Gateway middleware and Control Plane interceptors behind the existing RBAC v2 feature flags, and will add dashboards/alerts for cache hit ratio and evaluator error rates.

Testing: unit tests for cache key composition and revision pinning, concurrency tests (race), integration test against a stub evaluator (ensures headers and revision semantics), and a benchmark suite runnable with `bazel test //internal/authz/policyclient:bench`.

Risk: Low. The caching is opt-in per caller and defaults are conservative. If issues are observed, services can set `AUTHZ_POLICYCLIENT_CACHE_DISABLED=true` and/or lower TTL to 0 via config. All metrics are emitted so we can detect anomalous hit ratios and unexpected revision behavior quickly.

Refs: ENG-18388 (RBAC v2 rollout safety + perf), ENG-18277 (Gateway authz middleware foundation).
commits: authz(policyclient): add PolicyEvaluatorClient interface + HTTP/RPC adapter
authz(cache): implement scoped LRU cache w/ TTL + revision-keying
obs(metrics): add authz policy eval histograms/counters + span attrs
tests: add cache correctness + concurrency coverage; add stub evaluator integration test
bench: add policyclient microbench + gateway-style harness (non-prod)
conversation: Amara Diallo (review): Can we guarantee that role binding changes always bump `authz_revision`? If not, caching ALLOW is dangerous. Also, please confirm streaming endpoints will only evaluate once per request (initial headers) and not per chunk.

Jordan Lee (author): Yes—evaluator uses the bindings store revision + policy bundle version; any write to roles/bindings increments the bindings revision. I added an integration test that simulates a binding update and asserts the revision changes. Re: streaming, gateway middleware checks on request admission before streaming starts; not per chunk (separate PR wires it in).

Marcus Lin (review): Please add an explicit escape hatch to disable caching for break-glass / impersonation contexts. We should also ensure cache keys include subject_type to avoid collisions between user vs service principal IDs.

Jordan Lee (author): Added `Evaluate(ctx, req, WithCacheDisabled())` option and documented call sites. Cache key now includes `subject_type` and `authn_method` (human vs service) to avoid ambiguous IDs. Also default: if `ctx` has `authz.break_glass=true`, caching is disabled.

Ines Carvalho (review): Scope semantics—can you clarify how project/environment/cluster scopes are represented in the key? We should avoid different JSON serializations producing different keys. Suggest using a normalized string form.

Jordan Lee (author): Good call. Implemented `ScopeKey()` normalization: `org:{org_id}` + optional `project:{project_id}` + `env:{env_id}` + `cluster:{cluster_id}` segments, stable order, and empty segments omitted. Tests added.

Allison Grant (review): Metrics naming looks fine; please add units and buckets doc. Also we should emit cache size gauge and expose hit/miss as separate counters for easy ratio calculation in dashboards.
Jordan Lee (author): Added `authz_policy_eval_cache_entries` gauge; split hit/miss counters and documented buckets in `metrics.go` comment + `cmd/authz-bench/README.md`.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): Please ensure timeouts are conservative (don’t block request threads too long). Also add circuit-breaking behavior: if evaluator is down, we should fail closed but with a clear error surface to callers.

Jordan Lee (author): Client now defaults to 150ms timeout (configurable) and returns typed errors: `ErrUnavailable` vs `ErrDenied`. No fallback-to-allow. Callers can map `ErrUnavailable` to 503 with `authz_unavailable` reason code (follow-up PR will standardize error mapping in gateway).
CI: initial run failed due to gofmt and a data race in the bench harness; reran after fixes. Final status green.
Amara Diallo (review): Approved. Please make sure we add a dashboard panel for cache hit ratio during rollout.
Ethan Park (review): Approved; looks aligned with centralized evaluation decision and keeps service code clean.
